images.title: One ribbon, ten pieces
images.purpose: Show 3.9 m of ribbon cut into 10 equal pieces of 0.39 m, and one piece cut again into 10 pieces of 0.039 m.
images.composition: A long ribbon across the upper middle of the frame, one piece highlighted, with a zoom outline down to a magnified copy of that piece in the lower middle; one caption line at the bottom.
exact_structure: Top: a horizontal teal #0072B2 ribbon split by thin white gaps into exactly 10 equal pieces; a grey #6B7280 bracket over the whole ribbon labelled 3.9 m.
The first piece on the left is reddish purple #CC79A7, with the label 0.39 m just under it.
Two thin grey #6B7280 lines run from the ends of that piece down to an enlarged copy of it in the lower middle.
The enlarged piece is split by thin white gaps into exactly 10 equal amber #E69F00 pieces; the first of these is reddish purple #CC79A7 with the label 0.039 m under it.
Bottom caption, two short lines: 3.9 ÷ 10 = 39/10 × 1/10 = 0.39 and 3.9 ÷ 100 = 0.039.
rejection: the top ribbon or the enlarged piece not split into exactly 10 equal pieces
any length other than 3.9 m, 0.39 m and 0.039 m
the 0.039 m label placed on a piece of the full ribbon instead of the enlarged piece
images.takeaway: Dividing by 10 makes each piece one tenth as long, and dividing by 100 makes it one hundredth as long.
images.description: A 3.9 m teal ribbon cut into 10 pieces with one purple piece of 0.39 m, which is enlarged and cut into 10 smaller pieces of 0.039 m each.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on Anuja's ribbon cut into 10 and 100 pieces.
images.teaching_notes: Point out that cutting one tenth piece into 10 again gives the same piece as cutting the whole ribbon into 100.

image_decisions.why: The ribbon makes the size of each piece concrete before the fraction method is used.
